It seems `<label form>` was added in https://github.com/whatwg/html/commit/62b5a0e8a5401979e39444abd25b69266a198bf8

I can't find any email from that time discussing why it was added. I did find http://krijnhoetmer.nl/irc-logs/whatwg/20080903#l-1044 -- I suppose @Hixie studied implementations and found that `label` was a form-associated element, and for consistency all form-associated elements get a `form` attribute.

The `form` IDL attribute appears to be supported in WebKit/Blink/Gecko (haven't tested Edge). So removing it seems like it would be moving away from what is implemented.

But I did find a case that is not interoperable:
http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/3938
WebKit gives `null`, Blink/Gecko give `[object HTMLFormElement]`.
What is the motivation for removing it?

From @chaals' commit message I see http://chaals.github.io/testcases/MixedFormsTest.html which says

> With Yandex.browser 16.2, Firefox 44 and Safari 9.03, the form attribute on the label element does not determine in which form a control is submitted.

Though that's not what the spec requires to happen...

Granted, `form` on `label` is basically useless; it's not a "listed" element so won't be returned by any collection API. Form-association does have some complexity (c.f. `img`), and it seems (from the test in my previous comment) WebKit doesn't form-associate non-descendant `label`s in the parser (but does associate it [when it's a normal descendant](http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/3939)).

@domenic can you check what Edge does?

> Though that's not what the spec requires to happen...

Right, this test seems entirely unrelated to the spec; I'm not sure what the idea was.

> @domenic can you check what Edge does?

I can, if you tell me which checkboxes and buttons to push and what output to report.
For the record I wasn't for or against this. I mostly submitted this as to track through changes (not sure if that is happening at all elsewhere) and seemed a big change to deprecate anything.

Yep, much appreciated @jonathanKingston!

@domenic I was interested in the Live DOM Viewer tests :-)

| [descendant](http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/3939) | form | form | form | form |

@RByers, can you check what the stable channel usage for the two counters mentioned in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/787#issuecomment-191647492 is like?

> @RByers, can you check what the stable channel usage for the two counters mentioned in #787 (comment) is like?

Sure - from M48 over the past 7 days we have (as a fraction of PageDestruction):
HTMLLabelElementFormIDLAttribute: 0.01%
HTMLLabelElementFormContentAttribute: 0.006%

Thanks, @RByers!

@tkent-google, is this similar to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/294 in terms of the possible simplification? And given that the img case was left alone, would there be any wins from changing only label?

If we remove `form` content attribute support from `label` element, we can merge 'Listed elements' and 'Reassociateable elements' into one category.  https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#categories

> would there be any wins from changing only label?

As for the implementation complexity, it won't help much.  We can remove just a few lines of code.
If we changed the meaning of `label.form` IDL attribute so that it returns `label.control.form`, we would be possible to reduce more code.

> If we changed the meaning of `label.form` IDL attribute so that it returns `label.control.form`, we would be possible to reduce more code.

That seems like a nice idea, and would presumably be more compatible than removing the IDL attribute. The only likely case I can think of where it would break something is if a `label` doesn't have a control, but some script still expects `form` to return the form.

> The only likely case I can think of where it would break something is if a `label` doesn't have a control, but some script still expects `form` to return the form.

The first part in isolation ought to be common, with simple mistakes like `<label>thing:</label><input>`, perhaps because that got the styling right and associating them via ID is a hassle.

One could have label's `form` IDL attribute fall back to looking for an ancestor form element to cover slightly more cases.

I suppose I don't have a preference at all, except that interop is nice when it happens. @tkent-google, do you have a preferred course of action here?

We should collect data:

 a) `label.form` in the current definition returns a value different from `label.control.form`.

  If this value is ignorable, we may make `label.form` an alias of `label.control.form`

 b) `label.form` IDL access without label.control, and an ancestor `<form>` is the owner of the `<label>` in the current definition.

  If a) is not ignorable and this is a major part of 1, we should apply the second paragraph in the last @foolip comment.
  Otherwise, we may remove `form` content attribute support, but we should not remove `<label>` from form-associated elements.  It means non-ancestor association by parser should be kept.

Given the results in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/787#issuecomment-191637438 the chances of removing the non-ancestor association should be good, and collecting more data on the different options sounds great!

Google Chrome 50 has the counters.

> a) `label.form` in the current definition returns a value different from `label.control.form`.

It's 0.0001% to 0.0002% of all page views.  We can say it's low-risk to change the behavior.

> b) `label.form` IDL access without label.control, and an ancestor `<form>` is the owner of the `<label>` in the current definition.

It's 0%.  Probably `form` IDL access without asscociated control is 0%.

Thank you @tkent-google 

So the plan:
- Remove `form` content attribute from `label`.
- Make `label` no longer form-associated.
- Merge 'Listed elements' and 'Reassociateable elements' into one category.
- Change `label.form` IDL attribute so that it returns `label.control.form`.
@smaug---- @mounirlamouri what do you think about this change?
Is there anything a11y related we need to consider here?

In principle I believe a11y shouldn't be affected; there is still an association from a form to its controls and from a control to its labels, so for cases like

``` html
<table>
 <form>
  <tr><td><label for=foo>Foo</label> <td><input id=foo>
  ...
```

(i.e. where the `label` and `input` are not descendants of the `form` and so with the change the `label` is no longer directly associated with the form)

...it's still possible to go from the form to the label and back via the `input` element.

I don't know if browsers expose the form association to AT today and if so if any AT uses it for `label` in particular. I checked http://w3c.github.io/aria/html-aam/html-aam.html but it seems to mostly do things with the `label` <-> control association.

Maybe @stevefaulkner has more insights?
@dbolter, do you know perhaps?

I do not know of anyone who uses the form attribute on the `<label>` element on the AT side. In fact, this attribute would only make sense the moment when labels and associated form elements were no longer to be part of the `<form>` elements children. But as long as it is required that these be children of the associated `<form>` element, then I don't see a problem in deprecating the form attribute. The natural DOM hierarchy creates the explicit association by the form elements and labels being children of the form.
Thanks @MarcoZehe (and @dbolter). Sounds like we can move ahead unless @smaug---- has other unaired concerns.
I don't.

@MarcoZehe 

> I do not know of anyone who uses the form attribute on the `<label>` element on the AT side.

Great, thank you!

> But as long as it is required that these be children of the associated `<form>` element, then I don't see a problem in deprecating the form attribute. The natural DOM hierarchy creates the explicit association by the form elements and labels being children of the form.

The `form=""` attribute on form controls is intended to allow the controls (and their labels) to not be descendants of their form. As an example, consider a table with several columns where each row is a separate form, and the other columns contain form controls for that form. The way to mark that up in a conforming way is to use the `form=""` attribute on the controls; it's possible (but not required) right now to also do so on the `<label>` elements.

``` html
<table>
 <tr>
  <td>
   <form id="f1">
    <label>Foo <input name="foo"></label>
   </form>
  <td>
   <label>Bar <input name="bar" form="f1"></label>
  <td>
   <button form="f1">Submit form 1</button>
 </tr>
 ...
```

But as I said earlier, even in this scenario (and in non-conforming scenarios with misnested tags where the association is created only by the HTML parser), the `.form` _IDL_ attribute on a `label` element still points to the form if the `<label>` has an associated control of that form with the proposed change.

> But as I said earlier, even in this scenario (and in non-conforming scenarios with misnested tags where the association is created only by the HTML parser), the  .form  IDL attribute on a  label  element still points to the form if the  <label>  has an associated control of that form with the proposed change.

Then I don't see a problem at all. If the association via the for attribute on the label is missing, it's an author error anyway, and such an author is very unlikely to instead do the form attribute correctly. So if a label for association makes the form association, too, and automatically via the IDL, the association can still be retrieved if needed.
